prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B025 as a stand-alone prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Round 1 showed that all six of us reach the same names from different directions, but what matters is that the discovery chain is original and complete: proglucagon processing, the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, glucose-dependent insulinotropic and satiety actions, and receptor biology that made long-acting agonists a rational step. The mechanism has been confirmed for decades by independent groups, and outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease show a change in the field that is neither premature nor speculative. Holst covers secretion and physiology, Drucker the biology of GLP-1 and the therapeutic rationale, and Mojsov the active peptide form. That is the trio that anchors the citation in a discovery rather than a product, and it uses all three places. I considered whether a second part could be added and concluded that it would force one of these three out, which I cannot justify on the merits.
statement.case_against: The attribution weakness has not gone away after round 1, and I should say plainly that nothing in the supplied material lets me settle it. Priority for the active peptide is contested, Habener lies outside the credited names, and Knudsen, whose acylated analogues are why the discovery reached patients, is left out. If the committee decides that the citation must honour the therapeutic step, the physiological trio is incomplete and one name would have to give way. Choosing Mojsov over Knudsen is a judgement about what this prize rewards, a discovery that changes the field, and it is not a verdict that the translational work is minor. A second risk is that a prize this obviously deserved takes the place of cleaner configurations such as B045, though that is a reason to keep B045 close as an alternative and not a reason to dilute B025.

responses.point: Linnarsson moved from Drucker, Holst and Knudsen to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, but keeps Knudsen as a serious reservation and would move back only if the citation is meant to reward the therapeutic step explicitly.
responses.response: I welcome the move and agree with your condition. My view is that the answer to your question is the discovery side: the citation I propose says the physiology and the active form made incretin therapy possible, which tells the therapeutic story without making a company programme a laureate. I do not accept your point that translational chemistry has precedent as a reason to switch, because the committee would then have to say openly that this year's prize rewards the drug, and the attribution among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and Knudsen would be harder, not easier. I reconsidered the substitution after your response and keep my position, but I name Knudsen as the first name I would revisit if a majority wants a therapeutic citation.

responses.point: The chair asks that the committee examine the evidence on peptide identification before the final ballot instead of assuming Mojsov's priority, and agrees that B045 is the cleanest alternative.
responses.response: I share the request and I hold myself to it: the supplied material names Mojsov as credited for the active peptide, but it does not let me adjudicate her priority against Habener, and I will not claim that it does. What I can do is word the citation so that it does not assert priority in a contested step. 'Identification of its active form' describes the finding without ranking the groups, and that is why I keep it. If the committee thought that wording still overstated Mojsov's claim, the right response would be to reconsider the trio, not to hide the dispute. On B045 we agree, and I have kept it as my first alternative for the reasons you gave, with your point that its translation is still developing being a reason for patience.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius lists Knudsen as the first name to revisit for a therapeutic arm and keeps B031 and B051 as alternatives, while saying she is open to a second achievement beside GLP-1.
responses.response: On B031 I still read the principal achievement as the clinical demonstration that blocking TNF works, with the cytokine biology credited elsewhere, so I would not put it in a two-part prize at the cost of a GLP-1 name. Your question about a second achievement is fair, but any two-part configuration is capped at three people, so B025 would have to shrink to two names, and I find no defensible two-name GLP-1 core. I note your concern that the commercial success of the field may overshadow the science. I think the citation guards against that by naming physiology and peptide identification and not the drugs. My view on B045 as a possible second part has not changed, but I do not support it at that price.

responses.point: Sandberg treats CAR-T as the stronger clinical case than B045 and the missing Eshhar credit as a caveat, while describing B045 as the cleaner configuration.
responses.response: I read the case slightly differently after the first round. The chair's question was whether Eshhar's absence makes June, Sadelain and Rosenberg unworkable. I do not think wording can repair it: the conceptual origin of an engineered receptor, the costimulatory design and the clinical proof are separate achievements, and Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy is a different line of work from the receptor itself. That is why I keep B051 as a real but second alternative behind B045, and I disagree that the clinical strength outweighs the incomplete attribution. We agree that a method such as B050 does not solve the six-name problem by being impactful, and that a Hall-centred B001 would need its credit analysis made explicit first.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide is secure against Habener and others, which I cannot verify from the supplied material and have handled only through citation wording.
Whether a majority will want the citation to reward the therapeutic step, in which case I would revisit the third name in favour of Knudsen.
Whether B045 or B051 is the better second option if the GLP-1 attribution stalls, given the cleaner pair for UPR and the missing Eshhar credit for CAR-T.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name on the shortlist. I disclose my earlier nuclear-receptor co-authorship with Ronald Evans and my work with Johan Ericson, and my co-authorship with Per Svenningsson (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy) and Abdel El Manira (2009), none of which concerns a candidate. No recusal is needed.
